summary.short: Executive Order 14299 directs federal agencies, chiefly the Departments of Defense and Energy, to accelerate advanced nuclear reactor deployment for national security, including reactors powering military installations and AI data centers at DOE facilities, fuel supply, nuclear exports and prioritized nuclear security clearances.
summary.long: Executive Order 14299 directs agencies, chiefly the Departments of Defense and Energy, to accelerate advanced nuclear reactor deployment, fuel supply and exports for national security. Sec. 3 requires a Defense program of record and a reactor operating at a domestic military base by September 30, 2028. Sec. 4 directs DOE to initiate designating AI data centers located at or operated in coordination with DOE facilities as critical defense facilities, treats their electrical infrastructure as defense critical electric infrastructure, and requires DOE to authorize privately funded reactors at DOE sites, targeting operation within 30 months. Sec. 5 requires at least 20 metric tons of HALEU to be released to a fuel bank for authorized private projects. Sec. 7 directs NEPA consultation on categorical exclusions. Sec. 8 has State pursue at least 20 new 123 Agreements and DOE decide technology export authorizations within 30 days of a complete application, subject to concurrence. Sec. 9 prioritizes nuclear security clearances. The order is subject to appropriations, creates no enforceable rights and states no penalties.

notes: Text is the Federal Register publication (Vol. 90, No. 102, May 29, 2025) of an order dated May 23, 2025; the order is annotated as adopted. No enabling statute is cited. Internal tension: Sec. 1 refers to critical defense facilities designated under 16 U.S.C. 824o-1(c), while Sec. 4(a) directs initiating designation of AI data centers as critical defense facilities where appropriate, without citing that section. Sec. 10 subjects the order to budgetary and procurement processes and Sec. 11(b) to appropriations. Sec. 11(c) states the order creates no enforceable rights. Deadlines run from the date of the order. Sec. 8(e)(iii) refers to other Executive Orders without naming them, so no relation is recorded for them.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment was found. Numbers in the text are procedural deadlines (Sec. 3(a), 3(d), 4(b), 4(c), 5(a), 8(b)-(e)), a quantity sizing a government release duty (not less than 20 metric tons of HALEU, Sec. 5(b)), a policy target (at least 20 new 123 Agreements, Sec. 8(a)(ii)), and the 48 contiguous States and District of Columbia as the geographic scope of the designation in Sec. 4(a), none coded as thresholds.

enforcement.note: The order directs federal agencies (Sec. 3-9) and creates no penalties, fines, licence revocations, clawbacks or blocking powers. Sec. 11(c) states that it creates no enforceable rights for any party against the United States or any other person.
